Alertmanager alert HighRequestErrorRate (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/recommendation since 2026-11-26T00:58:21Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: HighRequestErrorRate fired for otel-demo/recommendation because every ListRecommendations call that reached recommendation failed on its downstream gRPC call to product-catalog's ListProducts, whose error text is 'failed to load products: failed to query products: dial tcp 10.96.47.129:5432: connect: connection refused'. 10.96.47.129:5432 is the ClusterIP of Service otel-demo/astronomy-db, and that database pod was crash-looping: the Deployment otel-demo/astronomy-db was updated at 2026-11-26T00:57:29Z (update manager "OpenAPI-Generator") to container limits cpu 5m / memory 5Mi with requests cpu 5m / memory 5Mi, down from a 100Mi memory limit in the previous ReplicaSet. The replacement pod astronomy-db-84b6f976bc-d6vn5 was OOMKilled (exit code 137, 5 restarts, BackOff events 00:58:09-01:00:34), postgres never finished initdb, the Service had only notReady endpoints, and the astronomy-db Deployment's available replicas dropped from 1 to 0 at 01:00-01:01. recommendation and product-catalog pods stayed running and available, so this is a dependency failure, not a crash of the alerted service. product-catalog (GetProduct/ListProducts ERROR spans, alert pending), frontend, frontend-proxy and checkout also show their own error signals in the same window; other otel-demo pods were ready with 0 restarts. All flagd fault-injection flags affecting product-catalog and recommendation read defaultVariant "off", and no NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota exists in otel-demo, so neither is the cause.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_available for deployment astronomy-db was 1 through 00:59 and 0 at 01:00 and 01:01, while the same metric for deployments product-catalog and recommendation stayed 1 throughout; Endpoints otel-demo/astronomy-db listed the pod only under notReadyAddresses with no ready addresses.
Before the change, the database was reachable: product-catalog's init container wait-for-astronomy-db logged 'astronomy-db (10.96.47.129:5432) open' at 2026-11-26T00:50:12Z.

The flagd configuration ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config has every fault-injection flag in its 'off' defaultVariant, including productCatalogFailure, productCatalogLockContention and recommendationCacheFailure, so no enabled feature flag injected a product-catalog or recommendation failure.

Other services show their own elevated error-span rates in the same interval (frontend 16.3/s, frontend-proxy 7.7/s, load-generator 3.9/s, product-catalog 3.9/s, checkout 0.71/s at 01:01), and one sampled trace contains recommendation's refused-connection error together with a frontend-proxy GET span with http.status_code 500 and a load-generator GET span with http.status_code 500.
All other otel-demo pods listed at 01:01:55Z were Running and ready with 0 restarts; astronomy-db-84b6f976bc-d6vn5 was the only pod not ready (4 restarts, last termination OOMKilled).
otel-demo contains no NetworkPolicy and no ResourceQuota objects at query time, so a network denial policy or namespace quota is not what blocks product-catalog from the database.

A flagd fault-injection flag (productCatalogFailure / productCatalogLockContention / recommendationCacheFailure) as the cause of the product-catalog and recommendation errors is rejected: all those flags are in defaultVariant 'off' in ConfigMap flagd-config, and the observed error text is a TCP connection refusal to the database ClusterIP 10.96.47.129:5432, not a flag-driven product failure.

An inherent postgres memory problem (memory leak) is rejected as the trigger: the Deployment keeps the same image postgres:18.4 in both ReplicaSets, the pre-change ReplicaSet astronomy-db-5db647df86 ran with a 100Mi memory limit and the database was reachable at 00:50:12Z, and the new pod with a 5Mi limit was OOMKilled (exit 137) already during initdb.

Review the reasoning for Deployment otel-demo/astronomy-db: raise its container memory limit (and CPU request/limit) back to a postgres-appropriate value such as the previous 100Mi memory limit and verify the pod stays Ready with no OOMKilled restarts and that Endpoints otel-demo/astronomy-db gains a ready address.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows Prometheus's state at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window; it cannot show the state when the incident happened.
